title: The Executive Sheet is the Crafter's source of truth and only the Core Facilitator may write to it
content:
A.1.10.2.1.1 makes the Executive Sheet the pivot of the whole Executive Process: "The Executive Sheet is the source of truth for the Spell Crafter who crafts the Spell based on its content. Only the Core Facilitator has write access to the Executive Sheet."

The write-access restriction is what gives the pipeline a single controlled entry point. The Crafter codes from the sheet, so anything not in the sheet should not be in the Spell — and only one accountable role can put something in the sheet. Combined with the Governance Point's duty to ensure every item is "justified by processes or structures ratified by Sky Governance" (A.1.10.2.2.1.2), this is the choke point where provenance is enforced.

The **input actions versus derived actions** split is a subtler control. Each executive action is "broken down into input actions (high-level actions) and derived actions (resulting from input actions)." Separating what was decided from what follows mechanically means a reviewer can check the derivation — a derived action with no corresponding input is a red flag, and this is exactly where unauthorized changes would hide, since consequential adjustments look routine.

Verification is distributed rather than concentrated: the sheet is "used by stakeholders, who are required to provide confirmation for proposed executive items," which is the Content Liaisons' function (A.1.10.2.2.3) — each confirming accuracy in their own area of expertise. No one person checks everything.

And it is an archive: "Past Executive Sheets are preserved in order to provide a record of Executive Votes and their provenance," one tab per vote, titled by Target Date.

The striking practical detail is the medium — "maintained on a large Google Sheets spreadsheet with several tabs." The source of truth for protocol changes lives in a commercial document whose access control is an application permission, not a governance mechanism. Access control, integrity, and history all rest on that platform's guarantees.
description: A.1.10.2.1.1 splits every executive action into input actions and derived actions, requires stakeholder confirmation, and preserves past sheets as the provenance record for each Executive Vote.
